te.sit:zuhd-food:0: ‘A'ishah said: The family of Muhammad ﷺ never ate their fill of barley bread for two consecutive days until he passed away.
te.sit:tanattu:0: Anas ibn Malik narrated that three men came to the houses of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ asking about how the Prophet ﷺ worshipped, and when they were told, they seemed to consider it little, and said: “Where are we compared to the Prophet ﷺ?” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said: “Are you the ones who said such and such? By Allah, I am the most fearful of Allah among you and the most conscious of Him; yet I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.”
te.sit:muadh-taweel:0: Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah narrated that Mu‘adh ibn Jabal used to pray with the Prophet ﷺ and then go and lead his people in prayer. One night he led them in the ‘Isha prayer and began with Surat al-Baqarah, so a man broke away, finished his prayer alone… When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Are you one who puts people to trial, O Mu‘adh?” — three times. “Why did you not recite ‘By the sun and its brightness’, ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’, ‘Read in the name of your Lord’ and the like? For behind you pray the elderly, the weak and those with needs.”
te.sit:bayyian-khiyar:0: Hakim ibn Hizam narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The buyer and the seller have the option (to cancel) as long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and make things clear, their transaction will be blessed; and if they lie and conceal, the blessing of their transaction will be wiped out.”
te.sit:tabassum-sadaqa:0: Abu Dharr narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Your smiling in the face of your brother is charity for you; your enjoining good and forbidding evil is charity; your guiding a man who is lost is charity for you; your seeing for a man with poor sight is charity for you; your removing a stone, a thorn or a bone from the road is charity for you; and your pouring from your bucket into your brother's bucket is charity for you.”
te.sit:umm-salama-dua:0: Umm Salamah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There is no servant who is struck by a calamity and says: ‘To Allah we belong and to Him we shall return; O Allah, reward me for my calamity and replace it for me with something better,’ except that Allah rewards him for his calamity and replaces it for him with something better.” She said: When Abu Salamah died, I said as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded me, and Allah replaced him for me with someone better than him: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
te.sit:jasad-wahid:0: Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, mercy and compassion is that of one body: when one part of it suffers, the rest of the body responds with sleeplessness and fever.”
te.sit:birr-walidayn:0: Abu Hurayrah said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah, who is most deserving of my good companionship?” He said: “Your mother.” He said: “Then who?” He said: “Your mother.” He said: “Then who?” He said: “Your mother.” He said: “Then who?” He said: “Your father.”
te.sit:ghirah-aisha:0: ‘A'ishah said: I was never as jealous of any of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ as I was of Khadijah, because he mentioned her so often… One day I angered him by saying: “Khadijah?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been granted her love.”
te.sit:khullah-abu-bakr:0: ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I were to take an intimate friend from the people of the earth, I would have taken Ibn Abi Quhafah (Abu Bakr) as an intimate friend; but your companion is the intimate friend of Allah.”
te.sit:gharib-dunya:0: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of my shoulder and said: “Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveller.” And Ibn ‘Umar used to say: “When you reach the evening, do not expect the morning; and when you reach the morning, do not expect the evening. Take from your health for your illness, and from your life for your death.”
te.sit:fasila-hope:0: Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If the Hour is established while one of you has a palm seedling in his hand, and he is able to plant it before it is established, let him plant it.”
te.sit:rifq-adam-intiqam:0: ‘A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never struck anything with his hand, neither a woman nor a servant, except when fighting in the cause of Allah; and he never took revenge for anything done to him, unless something Allah had made sacred was violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.
te.sit:rahma-atfal-aqraa:0: ‘A'ishah said: A bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Do you kiss your boys? We do not kiss them.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “What can I do for you if Allah has removed mercy from your heart?”
te.sit:jud-ramadan:0: Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most generous of people, and he was most generous in Ramadan when Jibril met him. Jibril would meet him every night of Ramadan and study the Quran with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more generous in doing good than the blowing wind.
te.sit:sabr-sadma-oula:0: Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a woman weeping at a grave, and said: “Fear Allah and be patient.” She said: “Leave me alone, for you have not been struck by my calamity” — and she did not recognise him. She was told: “That was the Prophet ﷺ.” So she came to the door of the Prophet ﷺ and found no doorkeepers there, and said: “I did not recognise you.” He said: “Patience is only at the first strike (of a calamity).”
te.sit:sidq-yahdi:0: ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man keeps telling the truth and striving for truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as truthful. And beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man keeps lying and striving for lies until he is recorded with Allah as a liar.”
te.sit:uhud-injury:0: Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet ﷺ was wounded in the head on the day of Uhud, and he said: “How can a people succeed who have wounded their Prophet?” Then it was revealed: “Not for you is the decision in anything.”
te.sit:al-ifk:0: The full story, with its long details, is narrated by ‘A'ishah herself: her long wait, and how the Prophet ﷺ issued no hasty judgement until revelation came declaring her innocence.
te.sit:anas-taakhkhur:0: Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had the best character of all people. One day he sent me on an errand, and I said: “By Allah, I will not go” — though in my heart I meant to go and do what the Prophet of Allah ﷺ had told me. I went out until I passed by some boys playing in the market, and suddenly the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of the back of my neck from behind. I looked at him and he was laughing, and he said: “O little Anas, did you go where I told you?” I said: “Yes, I am going, O Messenger of Allah.”
te.sit:sirr-anas:0: Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me while I was playing with the boys. He greeted us and sent me on an errand, and I was late in coming back to my mother. When I came she said: “What kept you?” I said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on an errand.” She said: “What was it?” I said: “It is a secret.” She said: “Do not tell anyone the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Anas said: “By Allah, if I had told it to anyone, I would have told it to you, O Thabit.”
te.sit:ghawrath-sword:0: Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said that he went on an expedition with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ towards Najd. The midday rest overtook them in a valley full of thorny trees. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stopped under an acacia tree and hung his sword on it, and we took a nap. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called us, and there was a bedouin with him. He said: “This man drew my sword against me while I was asleep. I woke up and it was unsheathed in his hand. He said: ‘Who will protect you from me?’ I said: ‘Allah’” — three times. And he did not punish him.
te.sit:da'in-jamal-afdal:0: Abu Hurayrah narrated that a man demanded repayment from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke harshly to him, and his Companions moved to deal with him. He said: “Leave him, for the one who has a right is entitled to speak. Buy a camel and give it to him.” They said: “We can only find one better than the age of his.” He said: “Buy it and give it to him, for the best of you are those who are best in repaying.”
te.sit:usama-shahada:0: Usamah ibn Zayd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us on an expedition… I caught up with a man and he said: “There is no god but Allah,” but I stabbed him. I mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Did he say ‘There is no god but Allah’ and you killed him?” I said: “O Messenger of Allah, he only said it out of fear of the weapon.” He said: “Did you cut open his heart to know whether he said it or not?” He kept repeating it to me until I wished I had only become Muslim that day.
te.sit:bukaa-tifl-salat:0: Abu Qatadah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I stand up for prayer intending to make it long, then I hear a child crying, so I shorten my prayer, disliking to make things hard for his mother.”
te.sit:janazat-yahudi:0: Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said: A funeral passed by us, and the Prophet ﷺ stood up for it and we stood up with him. We said: “O Messenger of Allah, it is the funeral of a Jew.” He said: “Is it not a soul?”
te.sit:yunus-hut:0: The supplication of Dhun-Nun (Yunus) when he supplicated in the belly of the whale was: “There is no god but You, glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.” No Muslim man ever supplicates with it for anything except that Allah responds to him.
te.sit:ayyub-sabr:0: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, hurt or distress befalls a Muslim, even the prick of a thorn, except that Allah expiates some of his sins because of it.
te.sit:ibrahim-abihi:0: Asma' said: My mother came to me while she was a polytheist… I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “My mother has come wishing (for my kindness); shall I keep ties with her?” He said: “Yes, keep ties with your mother.”
te.sit:abubakr-mistah:0: When Allah revealed this declaring my innocence, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq — who used to spend on Mistah ibn Uthathah because he was a relative and poor — said: “By Allah, I will never spend anything on Mistah again after what he said about ‘A'ishah.” Then Allah revealed: “And let not those of virtue among you swear…” … Abu Bakr said: “Yes, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me,” and he resumed the spending he used to give Mistah.
te.sit:khadija-wahy:0: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned with it, his heart trembling, and went in to Khadijah and said: “Cover me, cover me!” They covered him until the fear left him. He told Khadijah what had happened and said: “I feared for myself.” Khadijah said: “Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep ties of kinship, you bear the burden of the weak, you give to the destitute, you honour the guest, and you help those afflicted by calamities.”
te.sit:umm-salama-hudaybiyyah:0: When he had finished with the writing of the treaty, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions: “Get up, slaughter your sacrifices and shave your heads.” By Allah, not one of them got up, until he had said it three times. When none of them got up, he went in to Umm Salamah and told her what he had met from the people. Umm Salamah said: “O Prophet of Allah, would you like that (to be done)? Go out and do not speak a word to any of them until you have slaughtered your camels and called your barber to shave you…”
